title: Site derived tensor resolving data and canonical localization counit
statement: Let $(C,J)$ be a ringed site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with object, morphism and coefficient universes independent and $C$ essentially small relative to the coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention], and let $R$ be its commutative ring sheaf. Write $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}(C,J,R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal M)$ for unbounded integer cochain complexes, $K(\mathcal M)$ for their homotopy category, $D(\mathcal M)$ for a chosen-universe derived localization, $q:\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal M)\to K(\mathcal M)$ and $Q_h:K(\mathcal M)\to D(\mathcal M)$, with $Q=qQ_h$ and its fixed quotient comparison [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the canonical monoidal sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and its signed direct-sum total tensor $\operatorname{Tot}$ [def-sfb-monoidal-category]. Use the derived tensor $B_R$ of the published descent witness of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], and let the resolving-pair model map $r_{P,S}:Q\operatorname{Tot}(P,S)\xrightarrow{\sim}B_R(QP,QS)$, for flat-term K-flat complexes $P,S$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], be exactly the recorded representative comparison $\operatorname{tensorDescentPair}(P,S)$ [def-weil-pbc-tensor-descent-representative-comparison]: the inverse quotient comparison, the inverse chain/homotopy comparison, the resolving comparison of that same witness, and the quotient comparisons on both inputs. No new tensor, resolution or comparison is chosen. The canonical localization transformation $\varepsilon^R:(Q\times Q)B_R\Rightarrow\operatorname{Tot}Q$ is the unique natural transformation satisfying $\varepsilon^R_{P,S}=r_{P,S}^{-1}$ on every flat-term K-flat pair. Thus its existence and uniqueness are part of this specification, and its value is defined by this unique characterization on all complex pairs, with no flatness or boundedness restriction on the latter.

proof.text: Identify model with KFlatFixedTensor.representativeIso. Both use the same selected homotopy and resolving comparisons. The only additional factors in tensorDescentPair are the quotient-to-derived comparison maps; these are identities, so functoriality and the identity laws remove them.

Reuse the already proved total_comparison from the proof of lem-sf-ringed-kflat-single-tensor-comparison: its components on all complex pairs are normalized by representativeIso.inv on flat-term K-flat pairs. Use those same components for the desired natural transformation. The old naturality equation becomes the specified one by functoriality of the published bifunctor and by tensorHom_def for the ordinary tensor. The preceding model identification gives the required normalization.

For an arbitrary pair X,Y, use the functorial flat-term K-flat resolution F and augmentation π already constructed in the same comparison module. The source functor sends (π_X,π_Y) to an isomorphism because both augmentations are quasi-isomorphisms. Naturality of any two normalized transformations along this map expresses their components at X,Y through their components at F(X),F(Y). Those components equal the prescribed inverse model map. Cancel the invertible source map and apply natural-transformation extensionality. Thus the transformation is unique, without any flatness or boundedness condition on X,Y.

proof_origin.place: Tags 06YS and 06YU; reuse the proved total_comparison and functorial_resolution, identify the recorded model maps, and prove uniqueness by naturality and cancellation.
